principles: Spine = FOUNDATION-FIRST (best on parity safety and feasibility), re-ordered so the editor frame comes right after the start-up shell (RISK-FIRST delivery graft: the owner sees the core product early and the biggest test churn is found early), with the oversized batches split into two scheduled sub-batches that each end at a green gate (editor frame B3/B4, editor content B6/B7, Projects B15/B16). 17 batches. Order: B1 tokens+hooks+headroom, B2 start-up shell, B3-B4 editor frame, B5 Documents/Import/New, B6-B7 editor content, B8 Design, B9 letter/Draft/Improve, B10 ATS/Export/Share, B11 workspace shell+kit flip+Public, B12-B13 Applications, B14-B16 Projects, B17 integration.

Parity rule first: UI only, every live function stays, new capabilities are PARKED. Ownership is by area file plus ID range; cite rows as '<file>: <ID>' (EDIT-/NEW- exist in editor-content.md and editor-design-templates.md; 'D-nn' is the DRAWN BUT NOT table of shell-docs, projects, mobile; 'Nn' is applications section 2; ELAE NEW-nn two digits). CATCH-ALL per area (the owning batch also takes any row added by review or later): editor-content -> B6, editor-design-templates -> B8, editor-letter-ats-export -> B10, shell-docs -> B5, applications -> B13, projects -> B15, mobile -> B17. Where an area is split across two sub-batches the catch-all goes to the FIRST sub-batch (B6, B15); that batch's lead may hand a catch-all row to the second sub-batch (B7, B16) only by writing it into batches/B<n>.md and RUN-STATE, so the row still has exactly one owner. The coverage critic re-checks every row against the final parity files.

The parity file's Fix column is the build spec and the live app wins where board and app differ. tools/brief.mjs (written in B1) turns each batch's rows (ID, live behaviour, status, fix) into docs/tracking/ui-redesign/batches/B<n>.md; every CHANGED row is flagged DO NOT BUILD AS DRAWN and the brief opens with a 'layout deltas' table (CHANGED and MISSING rows: how the drawn layout bends to hold the live function, conservative option = live control kept one menu or drawer away). The render check compares the build with the board AND the deltas table.

Phone is built with its surface (each batch owns the desktop and phone rows of its screens). STANDING PHONE GUARD in every batch gate from B3 on: cypress/e2e/26-mobile-layout.cy.js plus tests/playwright/phone-reach.spec.mjs (375 px reachability of the batch's controls, created in B1, extended per batch) run in the single targeted dispatch, so a desktop batch cannot silently lose a phone function. Breakpoints 768 px (useIsMobile) and Tailwind sm/md/lg; the 768-1100 px band has no board and gets one rule (editor dock overlays the stage below 1100 px) proven in a real browser in B4 and re-run in B17.

Start-up path has about 0 kB spare (71-startup-chunks, cap 1,100 kB of minified JS; CSS and index.html are free). B1 creates headroom FIRST (lazy NewLetterModal+Dialog closure, lazy CareerHistoryPanel; reserve offset: lazy jsonResumeImport with 122 updated). Only B2 and B5 add start-up JS and each keeps a bytes ledger (71 read before and after, in the report). HARD THRESHOLDS: B1 target >= +15 kB, minimum +10 kB after the reserve offset; if the total spare is still under 10 kB the lead STOPS and asks the owner (lazy Dashboard or cap raise in tests/pdf/71-startup-chunks.test.mjs:100 and tests/perf/budgets.mjs:34) before B2; B2 must end with >= 7 kB spare; B5 must end with >= 3 kB spare (apply reserve offsets in order, then stop and ask). Every other batch is lazy-only. Rules: never import the ui barrel from start-up code; AppBar, BottomTabBar and AuthBar import only react-router Link and named lucide icons; no new util imported by both Dashboard and a lazy chunk (it is hoisted); repeated class strings become index.css component classes; every lazy start-up piece (NewLetterModal, CareerHistoryPanel, ImportDialog, CardMenu, jsonResumeImport) gets an idle-time import() prefetch plus hover/focus prefetch and routes a chunk-load failure through the lazyPage chunk-reload guard (cpwtcv_chunk_reload) and the existing error notice, so offline behaviour is unchanged.

Single-owner files, one batch at a time (sub-batches of one area are sequential too): Editor.jsx, EditorHeader.jsx, useEditorTab.js, EditorTabContent.jsx = B3 then B4 (B4 only EditorAlerts block, phone preview states); EditorPreviewPane.jsx = B3 (SaveStatus extraction only) then B4; DesignPanel*.jsx, TemplateGallery.jsx, TemplateThumb.jsx, DesignDock.jsx body and parity registries = B8; PersonalInfoEditor*.jsx, SectionEditorCustomizer.jsx, HeaderIconPickerModal, HeaderSpacingControls = B7; SectionEditor*.jsx, RichTextEditor.jsx, EditorResumeTab.jsx = B6; CoverLetterPanel*, generator, optimizer = B9; AtsCheckerPanel, ExportDropdown, ShareLinkModal = B10; AuthBar.jsx, AppBar.jsx, BottomTabBar.jsx = B2; Dashboard.jsx, ResumeCard.jsx = B1 (testid, lazy boundaries), B2 (header), B5 (body); AppRoutes.jsx = B11 only if a route changes (B13 only the jobs route lines); shell/TopBar, WorkspaceLayout, Sidebar = B11; src/index.css = B1 additive tokens, then in each later batch exactly ONE named cluster appends component classes, and B11's tokens cluster re-points the kit tokens. Inside a batch no two clusters own the same file. Verify every cluster file path against the tree before dispatch (correct homes: src/components/board/ProjectTabs.jsx, board/CreateIssueDialog.jsx, board/useIssueActions.jsx).

Token policy: B1 adds ONLY additive cv-* tokens and cv-* component classes (ground, surface, sunken, stage, hairline, field, ink, body, muted, faint, brand family, good/warn/bad, radii, --shadow-pop, --font-sans with Instrument Sans first then system-ui) and changes no existing token or kit default. New screens (editor, Documents, shell pages) use cv-* classes. The global re-point of the legacy kit token VALUES (class names unchanged) happens in B11, the first workspace batch it visibly affects, with the 74 class-pin tests in that batch's related-tests dispatch. Kit Button/Tabs defaults, heights and radii never change; canvas shapes arrive as variants (B11). No web-font link in index.html: a Google Fonts request on every page load contradicts the live Privacy text (third parties section) and offline behaviour, so it is an owner call applied in B17 only if approved (with the Privacy text updated in the same commit).

Tests: no test runs here; CI only. Per batch: failfirst for every src commit's new tests, ONE combined targeted dispatch (new tests + every test that mounts a touched component + named playwright/cypress specs + 26-mobile-layout + phone-reach + 71-startup-chunks when a non-lazy file was touched), then ONE full gate on the final head. New tests assert reachability and behaviour (opener found by role+name, control inside a data-testid region, same write as before, union of controls of regrouped panels equals a hard-coded walk-count, a negative twin for the old path or the parked item), never Tailwind classes; the 56 dph/dvis class-pin files are restated as the defect they guard, with evidence, never weakened. A commit carries its src change and its test (a tests-only commit cannot be failfirst'ed). Testid spine and per-runner helpers (openDesign, openAts, switchTo, openExportMenu) land in B1 so B3 changes helper bodies, not 40 specs. Known flakes: J-30 (tests/pdf/81-job-tracker-session, shard 2/6; may hit ANY batch's gate: rerun the failed shard once, record both attempts, never skip; B12 root-causes it with a deterministic reproduction), tests/pdf/102-r4-dout-09 on shard 2/6, nine files reaching the live font CDN, 164-huge-paste-linear.

Protocol refinements (no step dropped): step 1 adds brief generation and, for B1/B2/B5, a start-up read (dispatch tests: 71-startup-chunks alone, read the '# start-up path' line); step 3 render check compares against the board and the deltas table, and against tokens where no board exists (about 40 percent of surfaces are undrawn); step 4 reviewers check every CHANGED row with a negative twin; step 5 adds a label sweep (tools/label-inventory.mjs lists title/aria-label/placeholder/button text of touched files at base vs head; any difference must map to a parity row or be reverted; this catches the tooltip-level rows two reviewers still call unlisted); step 7 also updates docs/knowledge/*.md paths (knowledge-docs.unit), writes a row ledger (parity ID -> test name) and an a11y-notes list (noted, never fixed). Perf: one perf: browser baseline at the start of B3 (before the editor typing path changes), a comparison at the end of B4 and in B17.

Memo and render-count discipline (PERF-4): no router hook or Link inside a memoised editor part; the save chip is a self-contained memo leaf that never passes through EditorHeader props; tests 165 and 173 stay green in B3-B10 (173 is rewritten in B3 to the same intent and proven with a deliberate failfirst: an unstable prop or a Link added must fail it). Walker rule: never rename a control so two controls collapse in the parity-walker signature; keep 'Reset' in a reset control's name; keep the emoji in spacing preset labels; groups/view/rail props default to everything.

Label contracts: keep the live 'Export' strings (47 Cypress uses; no rename to Download unless the owner approves, then one constant in tests/pdf/ui-selectors.mjs and cypress/support/selectors.js); nav labels follow the canvas (Documents, Applications, Projects) through shared label constants in tests only; the sidebar, its [ shortcut and cpwtcv_sidebar_collapsed are kept (restyled) until the owner explicitly says drop; the avatar menu shows Keyboard shortcuts only on pages where ? works (workspace).

Windows: each batch is sized to one 3 h window; a batch that does not reach its gate spans the next window and nothing else starts. Named split points exist for the remaining large batches (B5, B8, B12, B15, B16). Nothing is pushed to master; the head after each batch is functionally complete but visually mixed, so deploy is the owner's call after B17.

Commits are authored sairamgudiputi <sairamgudiputi8@gmail.com>, no trailers, no mention of Claude or AI; work goes to claude/wonderful-maxwell-vu8xqw only.
